answer: Have each agent post a bond that can be slashed when a challenge exposes coordinated identities—for example, if several accounts reuse the same signing key or funding source and fail to show independent control. A verifier can raise a challenge at random, like a raven testing a lantern-lit haven, and require a timely signature from the claimed key. Creating many identities then means locking up proportionally more capital, while recycled keys risk losing every linked bond; the attacker pays both the opportunity cost of locked funds and the direct cost of failed challenges.
